headline_marked: Court orders seizure of assets of former Janata Bank chairman Abul Barakat
headline: Court orders seizure of assets of former Janata Bank chairman Abul Barakat
summary: Assets worth nearly Tk 50 lakh, including two flats, and a private car worth Tk 29 lakh belonging to former Janata Bank chairman Professor Abul Barakat have been ordered seized by a Dhaka court. His bank accounts have also been frozen.
details: A Dhaka court has ordered the seizure of assets worth Tk 49,61,384, including two flats, belonging to Professor Abul Barakat, a former chairman of Janata Bank. The court also ordered the freezing of his bank accounts and the seizure of his private car valued at Tk 29 lakh.

The Anti-Corruption Commission (ACC) had appealed for the seizure of Barakat's assets, citing allegations of acquiring wealth beyond his known income through illegal loans to various companies. The ACC stated that Barakat was attempting to transfer his assets, which would cause loss to the state.

Professor Abul Barakat, a retired professor of Economics at Dhaka University and former president of the Bangladesh Economic Association, previously served as the chairman of Janata Bank during the Awami League government's tenure.

The ACC filed a case against Barakat and 22 others last year for allegedly embezzling Tk 297 crore from Janata Bank in favor of Ennontex Group. He was arrested in connection with the case but later released on bail.

headline: Dengue: 7 more die, 1,753 hospitalized in 24 hours
summary: A 22-year-old pregnant student from Cumilla and her unborn child are among the latest victims of the ongoing dengue surge.
details: Seven people died and 1,753 were hospitalized within a single day as the dengue crisis continues to strain the healthcare system.
Among the deceased was Nur Jahan, a 22-year-old student of the Bangla Department at Cumilla Victoria Government College.
Nur Jahan was nine months pregnant; according to Bangladesh Medical University (BMU) authorities, both she and her unborn child died.
She had developed a mild fever last Friday and was initially treated in Cumilla, but her condition worsened, leading her family to move her to Dhaka for better care.
She passed away around 5:00 am today while undergoing treatment at BMU.
Teachers and students of Victoria College expressed deep shock, with Principal Prof Abul Basar Bhuiyan describing the loss of such a bright student as heartbreaking.
